articles.title: Jaipur-Ajmer Highway Horror: LPG Truck Explosion Sparks Massive Fire
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Rajasthan — A massive fire erupted on the Jaipur-Ajmer Highway near Dudu late on October 7, 2025, after a tanker rammed into a truck carrying LPG cylinders.

body.html:
Rajasthan — A massive fire erupted on the Jaipur-Ajmer Highway near Dudu late on October 7, 2025, after a tanker rammed into a truck carrying LPG cylinders. The collision triggered a chain of powerful explosions, with cylinders hurled hundreds of meters away and flames visible from several kilometers.

At least 4–5 trucks were destroyed. Initial reports varied — some noted one death, while others reported no confirmed fatalities. Two to three people, including the tanker driver, were injured and hospitalized. The drivers of the involved vehicles remain missing as search operations continue.

Firefighters and disaster teams battled the blaze amid repeated blasts, halting traffic for several kilometers. CM Bhajanlal Sharma and Deputy CM Prem Chand Bairwa oversaw rescue efforts and assured medical aid for the injured.

A similar LPG explosion on the same highway in December 2024 had killed 19 people, raising serious safety concerns once again.

articles.title: Mentally Unstable Man Lynched on Drone Theft Suspicion — 5 Arrested, Cops Suspended
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A brutal case of mob lynching has shocked Rae Bareli, Uttar Pradesh, where a 40-year-old man, Hariom Valmiki, was beaten to death by villagers after being mistaken for a drone thief. The incident began around 10 p.m.

body.html:
A brutal case of mob lynching has shocked Rae Bareli, Uttar Pradesh, where a 40-year-old man, Hariom Valmiki, was beaten to death by villagers after being mistaken for a drone thief.

The incident began around 10 p.m. near Gadganj, when police briefly detained Hariom, found him mentally unstable, and released him instead of taking him into custody. Hours later, as Hariom walked towards his in-laws’ home in Unchahar, he was stopped in Ishwardaspur village, where locals tied him up and beat him with sticks, rods, and belts for nearly two hours.

Eyewitnesses say Hariom cried out several times, even taking Rahul Gandhi’s name, but the mob continued thrashing him until he died.

Police have since arrested five accused — Vaibhav Singh, Vipin Kumar, Suresh Kumar, Anuj Maurya, and Sahdev, while two others have been identified from the viral video. The Rae Bareli police have also suspended five officers, including two inspectors, for negligence.

Hariom’s wife, Pinky, and his family have demanded the death penalty for the accused, blaming police inaction for his death. Authorities have assured that strict action will be taken against all those involved.

articles.title: Grandmother Elopes with Lover, Leaving Family in Shock — Jhansi Village in Uproar
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A shocking incident from Mauranipur in Jhansi district has left an entire village stunned. A 40-year-old woman, a grandmother of two, abandoned her family and fled with her 35-year-old lover, leaving behind her husband, children, and grandchildren in despair.

body.html:
A shocking incident from Mauranipur in Jhansi district has left an entire village stunned. A 40-year-old woman, a grandmother of two, abandoned her family and fled with her 35-year-old lover, leaving behind her husband, children, and grandchildren in despair.

The case comes from Saywari village under the Mauranipur Kotwali area. Kamta Prasad Adivasi, a hardworking villager, lives with his two sons, their wives, and two grandchildren. But his family’s peace was shattered when his wife, Sukhwati (40), suddenly disappeared from home, taking jewellery and cash with her.

According to the complaint, about two and a half years ago, Sukhwati had gone to work at a brick kiln in Bhind district, where she met Amar Singh Prajapati (35) from Bihuni village in Rath tehsil. Their friendship gradually turned into an affair. When Kamta Prasad learned about the relationship, he brought his wife back home. However, the two allegedly continued their contact over the phone.

A few days ago, while Kamta Prasad had gone to Jhansi for his son’s treatment, Sukhwati took the opportunity to run away with Amar Singh after stealing jewellery and cash from the house. When Kamta returned, both his wife and valuables were missing.

Heartbroken, Kamta Prasad lodged a complaint at the Mauranipur police station. Police have registered a case and begun an investigation.

Speaking to the media, Kamta said, “I never thought my wife would do this. We built our home together. There are small children and daughters-in-law at home, but she didn’t think of anyone. I just want justice.”

The incident has become the talk of the village, with locals expressing shock over Sukhwati’s actions, calling it a betrayal that has brought shame and sorrow to the family.
